chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the residents of the Sacred Mosque, he said: 'It is what is less than the prayer times up to Mecca.'
ai.seo_question: What is the geographical boundary for being considered a resident of the Sacred Mosque for Ihram expiation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the geographical boundary for the 'residents of the Sacred Mosque' (Hadiru al-Masjid al-Haram) to determine the applicable expiation (kaffarah) for unintentional violations during Ihram. By defining the scope as extending from the mosque's boundary to Mecca, it establishes that those residing within this zone are subject to different legal considerations than travelers, a distinction crucial for calculating the specific penalty for breaking Ihram restrictions.
